transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is… elevators, mostly. The slow ones especially, or if I’m in a small room and the door’s locked. My chest just jumps right away, like before I can even get my head around it, and all I can think is I need to get out.

It’s funny, years ago buildings didn’t seem to have so many of these little elevators—at least not the places I went—but now I notice them everywhere. Anyway, that’s the main thing. I step in and right off I feel like I’ve got to get back out.
When you’re in an elevator or a locked small room, is the main fear that you won’t be able to get out?

Yes, that’s pretty much it. I know a little storage room, or one of those elevators at the museum, isn’t really the same as being locked up somewhere, you know. I can tell myself that.

But the second I notice there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind just treats it like trouble. Like, “What if I can’t get out?” Even if part of me knows that doesn’t make much sense.
Outside of elevators and locked small rooms, do you also get this fear in other places where getting away might be hard, like buses, crowds, or being far from home?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way. I mean, buses… I haven’t ridden one much in years, not since I used to go across town, and that was a whole different thing back then. Crowds, I don’t love them, but who does, right?

It’s really when the door closes and I feel sort of boxed in. Like an elevator, or a little room where the door’s locked. Far from home… I don’t know, I haven’t noticed it being that exactly. It’s more that closed-in feeling.
Do you ever have these sudden rushes of fear when you’re not in an elevator or a locked small room?

Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, I can get startled like anyone—phone rings too loud, or somebody knocks when I’m half asleep—but that’s not the same thing, I don’t think.

It’s mostly tied to the elevator or when I’m in some little place and the door shuts. Otherwise… no, I can’t think of it just coming out of nowhere.
Do you avoid elevators because you’re afraid of being trapped in them?

Yes, I do. I mean, these days I’ll take the stairs if I can, even when my knees complain a little. At the museum, they sometimes have those archive jobs or little back rooms, and I’ve passed on helping with that kind of thing.

If I really can’t avoid it, I’ll ask a friend to wait nearby, which feels kind of silly at my age, but it helps knowing somebody’s right there if I need out.
Do you also avoid crowded places because you worry you might not be able to get out quickly?

I don’t think so, no. Crowds can be annoying, you know, people bumping into you, everybody walking like they’ve got nowhere to be and somehow still in your way. My wife used to say I got grumpy at the grocery store more than scared.

But worrying I can’t get out quickly… I don’t really think of it like that. If it’s crowded, I might leave because it’s irritating or too much fuss, but it’s not the same as when a door shuts and I feel closed in.
